Independent quartic-moment and leading cap-mass derivation in this review
correctness.rationale: The 2d caps are disjoint up to measure zero also at t=1/sqrt(2): a shared point has exactly two nonzero coordinates of equal magnitude. Sign flips and permutations make the linear concentration form scalar, and the sum of the linear coordinate squares shows its value is μ=σ(E_t). For degree two, the sign characters separate each x_i x_j and the entire diagonal sector, and permutations act on the trace-free diagonal form through a matrix with common diagonal and common off-diagonal. Writing a=∫_{E_t}x_1^4 and b=∫_{E_t}x_1²x_2² gives eigenvalues d(d+2)(a−b)/2 and d(d+2)b, respectively. Independently, the quartic H=∑_i x_i^4−3/(d+2) has conditional mean u^4+3(1−u²)^2/(d+1)−3/(d+2) on a cap with axis coordinate u. Integrating this mean gives ∫_{E_t}H=2d B_d T_d/[(d+1)(d+2)], since the weighted quartic is the negative derivative displayed in the proof divided by (d+1)(d+2) and multiplied by c_d. The identity a+(d−1)b=μ/d gives ∫_{E_t}H=d(d−1)(a−3b)/(d+2). Hence the gap is d(d+2)B_d T_d/(d²−1), and the multiplicity-weighted mean of the eigenvalues is μ; these recover both printed levels. The gap is positive since T_d≥(d−2)/2. Both E_t and its complement contain open sets, so a nonzero harmonic restriction has strictly positive squared mass on each. For δ=1−t², the caps centered on axes 1 and 2 give b∼4c_d δ^{(d+1)/2}/[(d−1)(d+1)] by integrating u²(1−u²)/(d−1); the remaining axes contribute one higher power. With μ∼2dc_d δ^{(d−1)/2}/(d−1), the trace identity gives λ_D∼d(d+2)c_d δ^{(d−1)/2}/(d−1). The quotient and its square root are exactly the two constants claimed. The argument works for complex coefficients with the stated Hermitian forms.
residual_risks: The narrow-cap limit fixes d. The proof is for pure harmonic degrees one and two and does not justify applying the same eigenvalues to a cumulative band or to the overlapping-cap regime.

value.rationale: The natural hyperoctahedrally symmetric mask provides an exact, quantified failure of second-moment isotropy to ensure stable quadratic recovery. Linear relative conditioning stays exactly one, while two geometrically identifiable sectors of harmonic quadratics are observed at different powers of cap width, with an explicit dimension-dependent leading ratio. The eigenspaces and gap explain which modes are poorly observed, beyond giving a counterexample or a few numerical values.
residual_risks: This concerns continuous relative conditioning. It is not a discrete sampling, absolute lower-bound, or noisy minimax guarantee.
